knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says to reassess whenever a new occupant, contractor, spill, electrical fault or weather change could invalidate the initial plan.
The go or no-go decision means work does not start if the job cannot be made safe within training and authority. The worker reports and waits.
The instruction says to check the work environment, product compatibility, ventilation, access, emergency exits and available equipment.

practicalCriteria: Identifies relevant hazards, scope and site conditions
Selects and explains suitable controls and methods
Performs the sequence without unsafe contamination transfer
Verifies the outcome and documents exceptions
Escalates situations outside training or authority
passRule: Assessor must observe every safety-critical criterion; any failure requires remediation and reassessment.
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 2: Verify site access, and check that exits and emergency arrangements are clear.
Record of procedure step 6: If the job cannot be made safe, isolate where possible, report the reason and wait for instructions.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 3 is not done: Check the work environment, ventilation, and any new occupants, contractors or hazards on site.
Stop work if procedure step 5 is not done: Make a go or no-go decision, and start only when the hazards are controlled within your training and authority.
Stop work if procedure step 6 is not done: If the job cannot be made safe, isolate where possible, report the reason and wait for instructions.
